hunks.baseline: From the day the imperial proclamation was posted in the streets, the area around the imperial palace grew busier than ever.
hunks.sol: From the day the imperial proclamation went up in the streets, the area around the palace was busier than ever.

hunks.baseline: The people, and their reasons for coming, were all different.
hunks.sol: People came for all sorts of reasons.

hunks.baseline: Commoners lingered outside the palace, hoping to catch even a glimpse of the ill-fated young prince they’d heard about only in rumors. Confucian scholars who fancied themselves men of loyalty and righteousness shouted at the top of their lungs, demanding to know why Prince Shangshan had been summoned in secret at a time like this. And poets and writers hoping to land themselves a position took the opportunity to compose and recite poems for the Emperor, who had finally secured an heir.
hunks.sol: Commoners lingered outside, hoping to catch even a glimpse of the ill-fated young king they’d only heard about. Confucian scholars who called themselves men of loyalty and righteousness demanded to know why Prince Shangshan had been summoned in secret at a time like this. And poets hoping to land a position composed verses for the Emperor, who had finally secured an heir, and recited them to anyone who would listen.

hunks.baseline: “You fool. Did you think His Highness would come out and say, ‘Oh, you’re here,’ just because we’re waiting? We’re only here because you never know.”
hunks.sol: “You fool. Did you think His Highness would come out and say, ‘Oh, you’re here,’ just because we’re waiting? We’re only here on the off chance he might.”

hunks.baseline: “Perhaps because they don’t share the same beliefs.”
hunks.sol: “Perhaps they disagree.”

hunks.baseline: “What? The Emperor having an heir is the Great Nation’s good fortune and a joy to all its people? It’s men like you, you toadies, who are ruining this country!”
hunks.sol: “What? The Emperor having an heir is the Great Nation’s good fortune and a joy to all its people? It’s toadies like you who are ruining this country!”

hunks.baseline: “Shut your mouth! How dare you say that in His Majesty’s presence… Right outside the imperial palace, of all places!”
hunks.sol: “Shut your mouth! How dare you speak like that before His Majesty… Right outside the imperial palace!”

hunks.baseline: “Disgraceful nonsense? Is that all you can say, you vermin who pretend not to see what’s happening right in front of you?”
hunks.sol: “How is it nonsense? You vermin can see perfectly well what’s happening, yet you pretend you can’t!”

hunks.baseline: “You son of a—Everyone! Words won’t settle this! Let’s drive those toadies out of the capital!”
hunks.sol: “You son of a—Everyone! Words won’t settle this! Let’s drive those toadies out of the Imperial Capital!”

hunks.baseline: The sight of hundreds of scholars hurling fists and inkstones at one another was quite a spectacle all on its own.
hunks.sol: Hundreds of scholars hurling fists and inkstones at one another made quite a spectacle.

hunks.baseline: “Hit him! Get him!”
hunks.sol: “Hit them! Hit them!”

hunks.baseline: Shouts and screams rang out from every direction. Someone watched the scene with their mouth hanging open, then muttered,
hunks.sol: Shouts and screams rang out from every direction. Someone stared at the scene with his mouth hanging open, then muttered, “The greatest contest since the founding of the nation.”

hunks.baseline: “This is the greatest contest since the founding of the nation.”
And it wasn’t the imperial guards watching the fight from up close with keen interest who stopped them.
hunks.sol: And it wasn’t the palace guards, who had been watching the fight unfold right in front of them with keen interest, who stopped it.

hunks.baseline: Amid the chaotic brawl, a scholar backing away with a brush gripped like a dagger felt something strange touch his back.
hunks.sol: Amid the chaos, a scholar backing away with a brush gripped like a dagger felt something touch his back.

hunks.baseline: The main road in front of the imperial palace was so wide that a hundred grown men could walk abreast without bumping shoulders. Besides, there wasn’t anything nearby that could be called a wall.
hunks.sol: The main road in front of the imperial palace was so wide that a hundred grown men could walk abreast without their shoulders touching. Besides, there was nothing nearby that could be called a wall.

hunks.baseline: One of the poets and writers, a pair of inkstones in his hands as he raced through the battlefield, charged toward the scholar—and suddenly froze. His mouth slowly fell open as he lifted his head.
hunks.sol: One of the poets, an inkstone in each hand, charged toward the scholar—and suddenly froze. His mouth slowly fell open as he lifted his head.

hunks.baseline: “Uh, uhh. Uh…”
hunks.sol: “Uh… uh…”

hunks.baseline: With a particularly heavy footstep, the scholar was shoved forward. He gulped, then turned around and finally understood.
hunks.sol: A particularly heavy footstep sounded, and something pushed the scholar forward. He gulped, turned around, and finally understood.

hunks.baseline: The thing behind him hadn’t been a wall at all.
hunks.sol: What stood behind him had never been a wall.

hunks.baseline: The air, just moments ago burning with the heat of a brawl, froze in an instant. By now, everyone gathered along the road in front of the imperial palace was staring, mouths agape, at the giant who had suddenly appeared.
hunks.sol: The air, hot with the brawl only moments ago, froze. Everyone gathered along the road outside the imperial palace stared, mouths agape, at the giant who had appeared among them.

hunks.baseline: A shock flashed through everyone’s minds like a bolt of lightning.
hunks.sol: The same thought struck them all like a bolt of lightning.

hunks.baseline: They had long since forgotten the sharp disagreement they’d been having only moments before.
People stared in stunned disbelief at a giant unlike any they had seen before—or would ever see again.
hunks.sol: The fierce disagreement of moments before was forgotten. They could only stare at a giant unlike any they had seen before—or would ever see again.

hunks.baseline: Even from a rough glance, he stood well over nine feet tall.
hunks.sol: Even at a glance, he stood well over nine feet tall.

hunks.baseline: His limbs were like pillars; a single swing of his arm looked as if it could raise a gale. The muscles covering his entire body like armor made people’s knees go weak just looking at him.
hunks.sol: His limbs were like pillars; a single swing looked as if it could raise a gale. Muscles covered his body like armor, enough to make their knees go weak just looking at him.

hunks.baseline: And what about that head, perched on his thick neck like a boulder?
hunks.sol: And what about the head perched on his thick neck like a great boulder?

hunks.baseline: Never mind that it was as big as a well-grown pumpkin. Every time those enormous eyes blinked, people felt as if their lives were being shortened.
hunks.sol: Never mind that it was as big as a well-grown pumpkin. Every time those enormous eyes blinked, people felt as though it took years off their lives.

hunks.baseline: The scholars who, only moments ago, had dared to demand an explanation from the Emperor were especially beside themselves.
hunks.sol: The scholars who had dared to demand an explanation from the Emperor were especially beside themselves.

hunks.baseline: *No. The Guard recruits from among ordinary people. That thing isn’t human.*
hunks.sol: *No. They recruit from among human beings. That thing isn’t human.*

hunks.baseline: *A secret weapon! The Emperor raised a secret weapon to wipe out his opposition!*
hunks.sol: *A secret weapon! The Emperor raised him to wipe out his opposition!*

hunks.baseline: If they were formally sentenced to drink poison or be beheaded, at least people would call it an honorable death. But if they took even one slap from that hand larger than a pot lid, they’d die like dogs.
hunks.sol: If they were formally sentenced to drink poison or be beheaded, at least people would call it an honorable death. But one slap from a hand bigger than a pot lid, and they’d die for nothing.

hunks.baseline: The scholar who would go down as the first person to discover the giant—and probably the first person to die at his hands—in the annals of the Great Nation’s scholarly world, barely managed to force out a voice that wouldn’t come.
hunks.sol: The scholar who would be recorded as the first to discover the giant in the annals of the Great Nation’s scholarly world—and probably as his first victim—barely managed to force out the words.

hunks.baseline: He addressed the giant in front of him, and the Emperor as well.
hunks.sol: He was speaking to the giant before him and to the Emperor.

hunks.baseline: There was right and wrong in all things, and a nation could stand only if it upheld the Three Bonds and Five Relationships. The scholar bit down so hard his lips bled as he thought,
hunks.sol: There was right and wrong in all things, and a nation could stand only if it upheld the Three Bonds and Five Relationships. The scholar bit his lip until it bled.

hunks.baseline: *I’d rather die here than spend what remains of my life cowering beneath the Emperor’s power!*
hunks.sol: *I’d rather die here than spend the rest of my life cowering beneath the Emperor’s power!*

hunks.baseline: If he died for a great cause, protecting Prince Shangshan and the world, it would be worth it.
hunks.sol: If he died protecting Prince Shangshan and the world for a great cause, it would be worth it.

hunks.baseline: His body trembled like an aspen, but his steadfast heart would break before it bent. He forced down his fear and looked up at the giant.
hunks.sol: His body trembled like an aspen, but his resolve was like bamboo: it would break before it bent. He forced down his fear and looked up at the giant.

hunks.baseline: Then he realized that hundreds of imperial guards had surrounded them. He knew death was coming.
hunks.sol: Then he noticed that hundreds of Imperial Guards had surrounded them and knew death was coming.

hunks.baseline: At least, until the commander of the guards shouted in a trembling voice:
hunks.sol: Until the guards’ commander shouted in a trembling voice.

hunks.baseline: “W-Who goes there?!”
hunks.sol: “W-Who are you?!”

hunks.baseline: “St-Stand there and identify yourself!”
hunks.sol: “Id-Identify yourself at once!”

hunks.baseline: The scholar, along with everyone watching, blinked and thought:
hunks.sol: The scholar and everyone else watching blinked.

hunks.baseline: In a voice as innocent as a child’s, he said,
hunks.sol: His voice was as innocent as a child’s.

hunks.baseline: In an instant, the tense atmosphere crumbled like a bowstring snapping.
hunks.sol: In an instant, the atmosphere, drawn taut as a bowstring, collapsed.

hunks.baseline: *He came to watch? He just came to watch?*
hunks.sol: *He came to watch? Just to watch?*

hunks.baseline: The voice rang through the hushed crowd. An old man with dark skin, barely five feet tall, shoved his way through the throng and ran over. He delivered a fierce whack to the giant’s thigh, then noticed all the eyes fixed on him and froze like a statue.
hunks.sol: The voice rang through the hushed crowd. A dark-skinned old man who barely reached five feet shoved his way through and ran over. He gave the giant’s thigh a sharp smack, then noticed all the eyes fixed on him and froze like a statue.

hunks.baseline: In the awkward silence, the commander of the guards looked back and forth between the young giant and the old dwarf, his eyes gone cold.
hunks.sol: In the awkward silence, the commander looked between the young giant and the old dwarf with a flat stare.

hunks.baseline: After a brief silence, the old dwarf answered,
hunks.sol: After a brief silence, the old dwarf answered, “An ordinary traveler passing by. Nothing more.”

hunks.baseline: “Just an ordinary traveler passing by.”
“You look awfully suspicious. Do you know each other?”
hunks.sol: “You look awfully suspicious. Do you two know each other?”

hunks.baseline: “Unfortunately, yes.”
hunks.sol: “Sadly, yes.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve no idea what that idiot thinks of me, but whenever he falls asleep, I try to strangle him. Sadly, I’ve failed every time.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve no idea what that idiot thinks of me, but whenever he falls asleep, I try to strangle him. Unfortunately, I’ve failed every time.”

hunks.baseline: The commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard looked at the giant’s neck, thicker than a bull’s, and murmured in understanding.
hunks.sol: The Imperial Guards’ commander looked at the giant’s neck, thicker than a bull’s, and nodded as if he understood.

hunks.baseline: Sharp spears and swords flashed in the tightly clenched hands of the guards. The old man let out a deep sigh at their menacing show of force, then spoke.
hunks.sol: Sharp spears and swords flashed in the Imperial Guards’ tightly clenched hands. The old man sighed at the menacing display.

hunks.baseline: The commander answered firmly, his expression and tone hardening.
hunks.sol: The commander’s expression and voice hardened.

hunks.baseline: “My companion has it, so that’s going to be a bit difficult.”
hunks.sol: “My companion has it, so that’s a bit difficult.”

hunks.baseline: “Then you’ll learn what a truly difficult situation is. And you say you have a companion? Is there another accomplice?”
hunks.sol: “Then you’ll learn what a truly difficult situation is. And what companion? Is there another accomplice?”

hunks.baseline: “He’s not an accomplice… Hey, don’t just stand there like an idiot. Go call your wet nurse.”
hunks.sol: “He’s not an accomplice… Hey, don’t just stand there. Hurry up and call your wet nurse.”

hunks.baseline: The guards nearby sensed trouble and hurried to stop him, but they were too late to prevent the giant’s shout.
hunks.sol: The guards nearby sensed trouble and hurried to stop them, but they were too late to prevent the giant’s shout.

hunks.baseline: The people filling the street outside the imperial palace were startled once by the immense shout that battered their ears, then twice by the strange words it contained.
hunks.sol: The people filling the road outside the imperial palace were startled once by the tremendous shout that battered their ears, then again by the strange words it contained.

hunks.baseline: *Is he really crazy?*
hunks.sol: *Is he actually crazy?*

hunks.baseline: Even the commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard was thrown into confusion.

hunks.baseline: Why was he shouting about five-spice pork out of nowhere? Was the name of those suspicious men’s accomplice Five-Spice Pork? Or had something gone wrong with his ears?
hunks.sol: Even the Imperial Guards’ commander was confused. Why shout for five-spice pork out of nowhere? Was Five-Spice Pork the name of those suspicious men’s accomplice? Or had he misheard?

hunks.baseline: But it was none of those things.
hunks.sol: It was none of those things.

hunks.baseline: The giant had simply shouted because he wanted to eat five-spice pork right then and there, and his companions had been through this kind of situation so many times they were sick of it.
hunks.sol: The giant had shouted because he wanted five-spice pork right then and there. And his companions had been through this sort of thing so often they were sick of it.

hunks.baseline: Put simply, they knew better than anyone that there was only one man in the world crazy enough to shout so loudly and desperately for five-spice pork on the road outside the imperial palace.
hunks.sol: Put simply, they knew better than anyone that there was only one man in the world crazy enough to call for five-spice pork that loudly and desperately outside the imperial palace.

hunks.baseline: And that this very man was their companion, who had wandered off while they’d looked away for a moment.
hunks.sol: They also knew he was their companion, who had vanished the moment they looked away.

hunks.baseline: At the urgent shout, the crowd parted like the sea drawing back.
hunks.sol: At the urgent shout, the crowd parted like a receding tide.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, the people who’d thought nothing could surprise them anymore had to rub their eyes once more.
hunks.sol: The people who had thought nothing could surprise them anymore found themselves rubbing their eyes again.

hunks.baseline: A carriage pulled by two horses was racing toward them at a mad pace.
hunks.sol: A carriage pulled by two horses was racing straight toward them.

hunks.baseline: The scene became a complete uproar. The carriage didn’t manage to stop until it reached the tense guards.
hunks.sol: The street erupted into chaos. The carriage barely managed to stop when it reached the tense Imperial Guards.

hunks.baseline: A young man jumped lightly down from it and hurriedly felt over the giant’s body.
hunks.sol: A young man jumped down and hurriedly felt over the giant’s body.

hunks.baseline: The giant answered with a goofy grin, like a five-year-old child. The onlookers shuddered again, but not the commander of the guards.
hunks.sol: The giant answered with a broad grin like a five-year-old’s. The onlookers shuddered again, but the commander did not.

hunks.baseline: He watched as people spilled out of the little carriage and thought,
hunks.sol: He watched people spill out of the little carriage.

hunks.baseline: *What is this group?*
hunks.sol: *What kind of group is this?*

hunks.baseline: A pretty girl with noticeable freckles, and a young man beside her with a face stiff as a log.
hunks.sol: A pretty girl with noticeable freckles, and a young man beside her whose face was as stiff as a log.

hunks.baseline: A giant who looked like a walking natural disaster, and a young man who handled that mountain of muscle as if it were a delicate piece of porcelain. An old man smiling placidly like an immortal amid all the chaos, and a short, dark-skinned old man beside him muttering curses.
hunks.sol: A giant who looked like a walking natural disaster, and a young man who handled that mountain of muscle as if it were delicate porcelain. An old man smiling like an immortal amid all the chaos, and a short, dark-skinned old man beside him muttering curses.

hunks.baseline: For some reason, even his eyebrows had been shaved clean off. He was a mean-looking, thoroughly disreputable monk.
hunks.sol: For some reason, even his eyebrows had been shaved clean off. He was a mean-looking, disreputable monk.

hunks.baseline: He guarded one of the imperial palace’s twelve gates and had seen all kinds of strange things, but he swore he’d never seen anything like this.
hunks.sol: The commander guarded one of the imperial palace’s twelve gates and had seen all kinds of things, but he swore he had never seen anything like this.

hunks.baseline: As the commander hesitated, bewildered, the mean-looking monk who had been the last to climb down from the carriage approached and held something out to him.
hunks.sol: As he hesitated in confusion, the mean-looking monk, who had been the last to climb down from the carriage, approached and held something out.

hunks.baseline: “What is this?”
hunks.sol: “What is this?” the commander asked.

hunks.baseline: “Ah, that came out wrong.”
hunks.sol: “Ah. That slipped out.”

hunks.baseline: As if trying to hold back his anger, the disreputable monk took a deep breath and continued.
hunks.sol: The monk took a deep breath, as if holding back his anger.

hunks.baseline: The commander hurriedly unfolded the letter in his hand. His eyes widened when he saw the seal of a high official—someone far beyond his station to question.
hunks.sol: The commander hurriedly unfolded the letter. His eyes widened when he saw the seal of a high official so far above his station he could hardly have looked the man in the eye.

hunks.baseline: He might only be a junior officer, but he was a hundred-man commander in the imperial guard, responsible for protecting the capital. To be spoken to like that by a troupe of traveling performers—
hunks.sol: He might be a junior officer, but he was a hundred-man commander of the Imperial Guards, charged with protecting the capital. And now a traveling performer was speaking to him like this.

hunks.baseline: But whoever backed this troupe was beyond anything he could handle. The commander swallowed his anger and ordered his men to open the gate, committing the troupe’s name, written on the letter, to memory.
hunks.sol: But whoever backed the troupe was beyond his ability to deal with. He swallowed his anger and ordered his men to open the gate, committing the troupe’s name on the letter to memory.

hunks.baseline: *The Blazing Flame Troupe? What a tacky name.*
hunks.sol: *The Blazing Flame Troupe? Even the name sounds tacky.*

hunks.baseline: Of course, it never crossed his mind that if he’d said that out loud, the monk would have beaten him half to death.
hunks.sol: Of course, it never crossed his mind that the monk would have beaten him half to death if he’d said that aloud.
